sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever typed the same number over and over in your code? Named constants are here to save you! Let's learn how to make your code cleaner and easier to update.

• What named constants are and why they're awesome
• How to declare them using the `final` keyword
• Real-world benefits of using constants in your programs

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're baking cookies and the recipe says 'use 3.14 teaspoons of vanilla'. If you had to write that number 10 times, you might make a typo. Instead, you'd write 'PI_TEASPOONS = 3.14' at the top and just use PI_TEASPOONS everywhere.

That's exactly what named constants do in programming! They let you:

• Give a meaningful name to important values
• Use that name everywhere in your code
• Change the value in just one place if needed

Here's how you declare a constant in Java:

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
```java
final double PI = 3.14159;
```

• `final` - This keyword makes the value permanent
• `double` - The data type (could be int, String, etc.)
• `PI` - The constant name (ALL_CAPS by convention)
• `3.14159` - The value that never changes

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Named constants are declared with the final keyword and cannot be reassigned
Constants improve readability by giving meaningful names to fixed values
Convention: name constants in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g., final double TAX_RATE = 0.07)
Using constants avoids magic numbers scattered throughout the code
Attempting to reassign a final variable causes a compilation error

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Named constants make your code more readable and maintainable. Always declare constants with `final` and ALL_CAPS names. Use constants for values that appear multiple times or might change. Practice declaring and using constants in simple calculations.

questions.question: How do you declare a constant in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, constants are declared using the 'final' keyword. Once assigned, a final variable's value cannot be changed. Java does not use the 'const' keyword.

questions.question: What happens if you try to change the value of a final variable?
questions.explanation: Attempting to reassign a value to a final variable causes a compilation error. The 'final' keyword ensures the value remains constant throughout the program.
